Skills-Checks (SC) nutrition
  • SC 1 children estimate how much they should drink per training session and check it (e.g. with markings on the water bottle).
  • SC 2 children independently check that all important items are packed (bag check).
  • SC Document and discuss one day of nutrition: food, drinks and snacks.
  • SC Independently put together a meal/snack for before, during and after training/competition and discuss it.
  • SC Experiment with different snacks, hydration strategies or meals before/during/after training/competition and adapt them individually.
  • SC 1 test nutrition and hydration under competition conditions (e.g. gels, isotonic drinks during exercise).
  • SC 2 document and analyse fluid loss, energy needs and recovery.
  • SC established nutrition and hydration strategy for training and competition.
Fluids

Goal

  • Promote healthy everyday habits
  • Involve parents with tips or workshops

Implement the sports bag checklist

  • Water bottle
  • snack box and change of clothes

Build conscious snack and drink breaks into training
Give explanations (per hour of training = 500 ml of water or diluted juice)

Cooking as a team

Joint snack preparation or cooking classes.

Goal

  • Basic understanding of balanced nutrition
  • Promote healthy everyday habits
  • Link between nutrition
  • energy for sport and school

Balanced diet

  • ½ vegetables/fruit
  • ¼ carbohydrates
  • ¼ protein at every meal

Drinking

  • Water as the main drink
  • approx
  • 1.5–2 l daily
  • more when training

Regular meals

  • Breakfast
  • lunch
  • dinner and 2 healthy snacks (e.g. fruit, nuts)

Preparation

Bring snacks and water bottle to training.

Goal

  • Strengthen awareness and adaptation
  • deepen understanding of macronutrients (carbohydrates, protein, fat) and fluid needs

Before training

  • Drink approx
  • 500 ml of water 1–2h beforehand
  • In heat or with high salt loss use slightly salty drinks (1 pinch of salt)

During training

Drink 150–200 ml every 15–20'; for efforts >1h add carbohydrates (e.g. diluted fruit juices, carbohydrate-rich drinks).

After training

  • 0.5-1 l of fluid within 30'
  • After intensive efforts use a protein shake
  • recovery drink
  • electrolyte drinks or slightly salty water

Optimisation and individualisation

Advanced knowledge of micronutrients (vitamins, minerals) and their role in performance.

Goal

  • Promote healthy everyday habits
  • Involve parents with tips or workshops

Implement the sports bag checklist

  • Water bottle
  • snack box and change of clothes

Build conscious snack and drink breaks into training
Give explanations (per hour of training = 500 ml of water or diluted juice)

Cooking as a team

Joint snack preparation or cooking classes.

Goal

  • Basic understanding of balanced nutrition
  • Promote healthy everyday habits
  • Link between nutrition
  • energy for sport and school

Balanced diet

  • ½ vegetables/fruit
  • ¼ carbohydrates
  • ¼ protein at every meal

Drinking

  • Water as the main drink
  • approx
  • 1.5–2 l daily
  • more when training

Regular meals

  • Breakfast
  • lunch
  • dinner and 2 healthy snacks (e.g. fruit, nuts)

Preparation

Bring snacks and water bottle to training.

Before training

  • 2–3h beforehand: carbohydrate-rich
  • easily digestible meal (e.g. wholegrain bread with honey)
  • 30' beforehand: small snack (e.g. banana)

During training (>1h exertion)

30–60 g of carbohydrates per hour (e.g. energy bar, dried fruit)

After training

Within 30': snack with carbohydrates and protein (e.g. yoghurt with fruit, milkshake).

Main meal

  • balanced with carbohydrates (e.g. rice, pasta)
  • protein (e.g. chicken, lentils) and vegetables

Optimisation and individualisation

Advanced knowledge of micronutrients (vitamins, minerals) and their role in performance.

Skills-Checks (SC) sleep
  • SC Questions for the children: how many hours of sleep do we need? What helps us sleep better?
  • SC For one week, document sleep duration and how they feel the next day.
  • SC Try breathing techniques or progressive muscle relaxation (PMR) before sleep.
  • SC 1 document sleep duration and quality for one week, together with training performance.
  • SC 2 reflect on evening routines and make adjustments.
  • SC 1 create and implement a plan for sleep and meal times before a competition.
  • SC 2 "park" thoughts before sleep, e.g. by writing them down or with breathing exercises (rumination stop)
  • SC established sleep routine for training and competition.
Sleep content

Sleep duration

8–10h/night
Sleep supports concentration, energy and recovery.

Sleep duration

8–10h/night

Routine

Same bedtimes, also at weekends.

Relaxation

  • Avoid screens 1h before sleep
  • introduce rituals such as reading or breathing exercises

Sleep environment

  • Dark
  • cool
  • quiet (16–18°C)
Gesundheit & Entwicklung T1-M

Regular sleep times

Build in relaxation rituals

Rumination stop

  • Get up if awake for a long time
  • Write down thoughts to clear your head
  • Turn negative thoughts about sleep into positive beliefs

Optimised use of caffeine and aids

  • Consider the effect (half-life 6h, stronger effect in adolescents)
  • avoid at least 6h before sleep
  • Use eye masks
  • ear protection
  • etc

Plan power naps

  • Short naps of 10–15' for recovery
  • ideally after lunch

Adjustments for travel and competitions

  • Adapt sleep and meal times to time zone changes
  • Use strategies against jet lag
Gesundheit & Entwicklung T1-M

Targeted and individual sleep optimisation secures long-term performance.

Regular sleep routines and adapting to travel or competitions are decisive.

  • Sleep problems should be monitored and treated if necessary
  • Power naps and relaxation techniques such as the rumination stop promote recovery and mental calm
Gesundheit & Entwicklung T1-M

Skills-Checks (SC) mental skills
  • SC Athletes talk about a moment they are proud of.
  • SC Athletes describe their emotions in difficult situations (e.g. after a mistake) using a traffic light.

Red

I am angry.

Yellow

I am unsure.

Green

I am calm/focused.

  • SC Athletes perform a task (e.g. technique exercise) with distractions (e.g. noise): test the ability to stay focused.
  • SC 1 Athletes formulate a small goal for training and explain why it matters to them.
  • SC 2 Simulated stress situation (e.g. competition simulation). Children consciously use techniques (e.g. breathing) to reach 'green'.
  • SC Athletes describe a best performance: 'How did you feel?': identify and apply the characteristics of the personal optimal performance state.
  • SC 1 for each category, process goals and ranking goals (evaluate and adjust later).
  • SC 2 during e.g. interval training, consciously use breathing techniques to stay calm.
  • SC 3 before a technique task, mentally rehearse the sequence.
  • SC 1 For each category, process goals and ranking goals (evaluate and adjust later).
  • SC 2 Use positive self-talk in a difficult task (e.g. time pressure).
  • SC 3 Perform a technique exercise with built-in distractions.
  • SC1 apply an established mental activation routine before competition.
  • SC2 use targeted breathing techniques or self-talk in pressure situations.
  • SC3 after a setback, consciously direct focus to the next task.
  • SC4 specifically visualise an upcoming competition situation.

F3 Inhalt

Training is adapted to the athletes' performance level

Preparation phase 1

  • Barbell technique with bodyweight and light additional loads
  • First jump forms (focus on correct landing technique)
  • Core stability training

Preparation phase 2

  • Muscle building
  • Building up explosive strength training
  • Core training

Pre-competition phase

  • Explosive strength training
  • Core training

Competition phase

  • Explosive strength training & plyometrics at reduced volume
  • Maintaining core training

* Window of opportunity in girls T1
* Window of opportunity in boys T2

T1 InhaltT2 Inhalt

Training is adapted to the athletes' performance level and split into upper body and lower body

Preparation phase 1

  • Develop functional efficiency (barbell technique)
  • Plyometric exercises to promote explosiveness
  • Core training

Preparation phase 2

  • Build muscle potential (muscle hypertrophy)
  • Increase maximum strength through intramuscular coordination training (express muscle potential)
  • Explosive strength training with additional loads
  • Core training

Pre-competition phase

  • Increase maximum strength through intramuscular coordination training (express muscle potential)
  • Training speed & explosive strength with and without additional load
  • Core training

Competition phase

  • Maintain explosive and maximum strength
  • Adapting volume to competitions
  • Intensity remains

parallel turns

skating step on the flat
waltz

skiing in a defined space (pole forest)

one-legged turns on an easy slope
parallel turn switch (skidded)
efficient skating step
waltz

piste trick (180°, powerslide)

Recovery April to mid-May
–

Goals

Ensure physical and mental recovery after the competition season and revive the joy of multi-sport movement.

Content

  • Unstructured
  • playful movement in everyday life (cycling, swimming, game sports) with clearly reduced training volume and without cross-country-specific content

Goals

Ensure recovery from the competition season and maintain the joy of sport through multi-sport movement.

Content

  • Unstructured
  • varied activities without cross-country-specific content (cycling, swimming, game sports) with clearly reduced volume

Goals

Ensure physical and mental recovery after the competition season and maintain training enjoyment through multi-sport movement.

Content

  • Unstructured
  • varied activities without cross-country-specific content (cycling, swimming, game sports) at clearly reduced volume

Goals

Ensure physical and mental recovery after the intensive competition season and prevent load monotony through multi-sport movement.

Content

  • Unstructured
  • varied activities without cross-country-specific content (cycling, swimming, game sports) at clearly reduced volume and low intensity

Goals

Ensure physical and mental recovery after the intensive competition season and prevent load monotony and overtraining.

Content

  • Unstructured
  • varied activities without cross-country-specific content (cycling, swimming, game sports) at clearly reduced volume and low intensity

Goals

Ensure physical and mental recovery after the international competition season and prevent overtraining.

Content

  • Unstructured
  • varied activities without cross-country-specific content (cycling, swimming, game sports) at clearly reduced volume and low intensity

Goals

Ensure physical and mental recovery after the World Cup season and prevent overtraining at the highest load level.

Content

  • Unstructured
  • varied activities without cross-country-specific content (cycling, swimming, game sports) at clearly reduced volume and low intensity
Preparation phase 1 Mid-May to August

Develop basic movement and game forms

  • Extensive
  • varied and challenging

Goals

  • Build load tolerance extensively and in a varied way
  • and consolidate athletic basics (coordination, mobility, basic strength)

Content

  • Multi-sport athletic training (~6.4 h/week) with running drills
  • jumps
  • bodyweight exercises
  • barbell technique training as well as first roller ski sessions to learn basic classic and skating movements

Goals

  • Build broad training foundations
  • increase volume and frequency
  • and encourage cross-sport versatility

Content

  • Athletic training focusing on barbell technique
  • core stability and first jump forms (~6.2 h/week)
  • combined with cycling
  • running
  • swimming and complementary sports such as athletics or gymnastics

Goals

Build broad training foundations and increase volume and frequency to a clearly higher level.

Content

  • Multi-sport athletic training with barbell technique
  • core stability and jump school (~7.7 h/week)
  • combined with cycling
  • running
  • swimming and complementary sports such as biking
  • athletics or gymnastics

Goals

Build conditioning foundations broadly and sustainably and increase volume and frequency at a high level.

Content

  • Multi-sport athletic training (~9.1 h/week) focusing on functional efficiency
  • barbell technique
  • plyometrics and core strength
  • combined with base endurance on the bike
  • running and roller skis at low to medium intensity

Goals

Build conditioning foundations broadly and sustainably and increase volume and frequency at a high level.

Content

  • Extensive athletic training (~9.8 h/week) focusing on functional efficiency
  • barbell technique
  • plyometrics and core strength
  • combined with base endurance on the bike
  • running and roller skis at low to medium intensity

Goals

Build conditioning foundations broadly and sustainably at a high volume level (18–22 h/week).

Content

  • Endurance training on foot and on roller skis
  • supplemented by cycling
  • rowing and swimming
  • combined with two intensive sessions per week (I4/I5) and athletic training (~11.7 h/week) focusing on barbell technique
  • plyometrics and core strength

Goals

Build conditioning foundations broadly and sustainably at the highest volume level (18–22 h/week).

Content

  • Endurance training on foot and on roller skis
  • supplemented by cycling
  • rowing and swimming
  • combined with two intensive sessions per week (I4/I5) and athletic training (~13.4 h/week) focusing on barbell technique
  • plyometrics and core strength

Goals

Develop conditioning foundations at world-class level and specifically develop individual needs.

Content

  • High-volume endurance training on foot and on roller skis with specific training equipment
  • supplemented by cycling
  • rowing and swimming as well as athletic training (~14.2 h/week) focusing on barbell technique
  • plyometrics and core strength
Preparation phase 2 September to October

Develop basic movement and game forms

  • Extensive
  • varied and challenging

Goals

Consolidate sport-specific movement quality on roller skis and specifically use the speed/agility windows.

Content

  • Increased share of roller skiing (classic and skating) with focus on leg push-off
  • double poling and 1:2 technique
  • supplemented by sprint
  • coordination and jump forms as well as more advanced strength training

Goals

  • Consolidate base endurance (I1) and sport-specific technique
  • and specifically develop speed and muscle growth

Content

  • Structured endurance sessions (mountain and cross running, cycling 60–120')
  • roller skiing with technique focus as well as muscle building
  • beginning explosive strength training and core strength

Goals

  • Specifically develop base endurance (I1)
  • sport-specific technique and muscle growth
  • and use speed according to the window of opportunity (especially in boys)

Content

  • Structured endurance sessions (mountain and cross running, cycling 60–120')
  • roller skiing with technique focus as well as muscle building
  • beginning explosive strength training and core strength

Goals

  • Specifically develop threshold
  • capacity and maximum strength
  • and sharpen the individual athlete profile

Content

  • Structured threshold blocks (I2/I3) supplemented by capacity training
  • muscle hypertrophy and intramuscular coordination training
  • combined with roller ski technique and first national roller ski races

Goals

  • Specifically develop threshold
  • capacity and maximum strength
  • and further sharpen the individual athlete profile

Content

  • Structured threshold blocks (I2/I3) supplemented by capacity training
  • muscle hypertrophy and intramuscular coordination training
  • combined with roller ski technique as well as 2–4 national roller ski races and cross-country training races

Goals

  • Specifically develop VO₂max and base endurance
  • and further build muscle hypertrophy and maximum strength

Content

  • Endurance and interval training on the roller ski track
  • supplemented by summer competitions (1–2 roller ski races, cross-country training races) as well as intramuscular coordination training and explosive strength training with additional loads

Goals

  • Specifically develop VO₂max and base endurance
  • and further build muscle hypertrophy and maximum strength

Content

  • Endurance and interval training on the roller ski track
  • supplemented by 2–4 national/international roller ski races and cross-country training races as well as intramuscular coordination training and explosive strength training with additional loads

Goals

  • Develop VO₂max
  • lactate tolerance and threshold speed at world-class level
  • and further build muscle hypertrophy and maximum strength

Content

  • Endurance and interval training on the roller ski track
  • supplemented by 2–4 national/international roller ski races and cross-country training races as well as intramuscular coordination training and explosive strength training with additional loads
Pre-competition phase November

Develop basic movement and game forms

  • Extensive
  • varied and challenging

Goals

  • Manage the transition from roller skis to snow and establish playful
  • safe movement on cross-country skis (classic and skating)

Content

  • First snow sessions with game forms (elephant washing, hospital tag, skills park)
  • basic techniques (diagonal stride, herringbone, step turning, 1:2) as well as maintaining athletics through short
  • intensive sessions and varied jumps

Goals

Refine technique on roller skis and snow and prepare the transition to the snow season.

Content

  • Technique courses on roller skis
  • running with poles in rolling terrain
  • games and relays as well as explosive strength and core strength training

Goals

  • Refine technique on roller skis and snow
  • develop explosive strength and prepare the transition to the snow season

Content

  • Technique courses on roller skis
  • running with poles in rolling terrain
  • games and relays as well as explosive strength and core strength training

Goals

Manage form through short intervals and bring maximum and speed strength to season level.

Content

  • Continuation of all training forms with emphasis on short intervals
  • speed and explosive strength with and without additional load
  • and transition to snow with technique focus

Goals

Manage form through short intervals and bring maximum and speed strength to season level.

Content

  • Continuation of all training forms with emphasis on short intervals
  • speed and explosive strength with and without additional load
  • and transition to snow with technique focus

Goals

Bring race intensity and VO₂max to competition level and adapt them on snow.

Content

  • Training on snow and skis with race-pace intervals
  • supplemented by speed and explosive strength training as well as core strength

Goals

Bring race intensity and VO₂max to World Cup level and adapt them on snow.

Content

  • Training on snow and skis with race-pace intervals
  • supplemented by speed and explosive strength training as well as core strength

Goals

Bring pace endurance and high-speed technique to World Cup level and adapt them on snow.

Content

  • Training on snow and skis with race-pace intervals
  • supplemented by speed and explosive strength training as well as core strength
Competition phase December to March

Develop basic movement and game forms

  • Extensive
  • varied and challenging

Goals

  • Gain first competition experience in a joyful
  • learning-oriented environment and apply the movement quality built up in summer on snow

Content

  • Regular snow training with technical variety
  • participation in local/regional events and the Swiss Nordic Trophy
  • supplemented by reduced athletic training (~2.6 h/week) for strength maintenance and injury prevention

Goals

Use the roughly six months of snow time intensively for technique and foundation training and gain experience through regional competitions.

Content

  • Lots of time on skis focusing on technique
  • descents
  • games and coordination
  • supplemented by maintaining athletic and core training (~2.6 h/week) as well as reduced explosive strength training and plyometrics

Goals

Use the roughly six months of snow time intensively for technique and foundation training and gain experience through regional and international competitions.

Content

  • Lots of time on skis focusing on technique
  • descents
  • games and coordination
  • supplemented by maintaining athletic and core training (~2.6 h/week) as well as explosive strength training and plyometrics at reduced volume

Goals

Use the roughly six months of snow time for form and performance management in a dense competition calendar.

Content

  • Lots of time on skis with foundation and technique training despite performance dips
  • form management through short and combined intervals as well as maintaining athletic
  • explosive and maximum strength training (~2.6 h/week) with volume adapted to competitions

Goals

Use the roughly six months of snow time for targeted form and performance management in the dense international competition calendar.

Content

  • Lots of time on skis with foundation and technique training despite performance dips
  • form management through short and combined intervals as well as maintaining athletic
  • explosive and maximum strength training (~3.3 h/week) with volume adapted to competitions

Goals

Deliver competition performance in the international calendar and manage form through targeted tapering.

Content

  • Competition-oriented ski training with individual load management
  • combined with maintaining athletic
  • explosive and maximum strength training (~3.8 h/week) at constant intensity and volume adapted to competitions

  • SC 1 Children estimate how much they should drink per training session and check it (e.g. with markings on the water bottle).

  • SC Experiment with different snacks, hydration strategies or meals before/during/after training/competition and adapt them individually.

Nutrition

Goal

  • Strengthen awareness and adaptation
  • deepen understanding of macronutrients (carbohydrates, protein, fat) and fluid needs

Before training

  • Drink approx
  • 500 ml of water 1–2h beforehand
  • In heat or with high salt loss use slightly salty drinks (1 pinch of salt)

During training

Drink 150–200 ml every 15–20'; for efforts >1h add carbohydrates (e.g. diluted fruit juices, carbohydrate-rich drinks).

After training

  • 0.5-1 l of fluid within 30'
  • After intensive efforts use a protein shake
  • recovery drink
  • electrolyte drinks or slightly salty water

Advanced knowledge of micronutrients (vitamins, minerals) and their role in performance.

Nutrition

Before training

  • 2–3h beforehand: carbohydrate-rich
  • easily digestible meal (e.g. wholegrain bread with honey)
  • 30' beforehand: small snack (e.g. banana)

During training (>1h exertion)

30–60 g of carbohydrates per hour (e.g. energy bar, dried fruit)

After training

Within 30': snack with carbohydrates and protein (e.g. yoghurt with fruit, milkshake).

Main meal

  • balanced with carbohydrates (e.g. rice, pasta)
  • protein (e.g. chicken, lentils) and vegetables

Skills-Check (SC)
  • SC Questions for the children: how many hours of sleep do we need? What helps us sleep better?
  • SC For one week, document sleep duration and how they feel the next day.
  • SC Try breathing techniques or progressive muscle relaxation (PMR) before sleep.
  • SC 1 Document sleep duration and quality for one week, together with training performance.
  • SC 2 Reflect on evening routines and make adjustments.
  • SC 1 Create and implement a plan for sleep and meal times before a competition.
  • SC 2 'Park' thoughts before sleep, e.g. by writing them down or with breathing exercises (rumination stop)
  • SC Established sleep routine for training and competition.
Content

Sleep duration

8–10h/night
Sleep supports concentration, energy and recovery.

Sleep

Sleep duration

8–10h/night

Routine

Same bedtimes, also at weekends.

Relaxation

  • Avoid screens 1h before sleep
  • introduce rituals such as reading or breathing exercises

Sleep environment

  • Dark
  • cool
  • quiet (16–18°C)
Sleep

Regular sleep times

Build in relaxation rituals

Thought stop

  • Get up if awake for a long time
  • Write down thoughts to clear the mind
  • Turn negative thoughts about sleep into positive beliefs

Optimised use of caffeine and aids

  • Consider the effect (half-life 6h, stronger effect in adolescents)
  • avoid at least 6h before sleep
  • Use eye masks
  • ear protection
  • etc

Plan power naps

  • Short naps of 10–15' for recovery
  • ideally after lunch

Adjustments for travel and competitions

  • Adapt sleep and meal times to time zone changes
  • Use strategies against jet lag
Sleep
  • Targeted
  • individual sleep optimisation secures long-term performance

Regular sleep routines and adaptation to travel or competitions are decisive.

  • Sleep problems should be monitored and treated if necessary
  • Power naps and relaxation techniques such as the thought stop promote recovery and mental calm

Skills-Checks (SC) mental skills
  • SC Athletes talk about a moment they are proud of.
  • SC Athletes describe their emotions in difficult situations (e.g. after a mistake) using a traffic light.

Red

I am angry.

Yellow

I am unsure.

Green

I am calm/focused.

  • SC Athletes perform a task (e.g. technique exercise) with distractions (e.g. noise): test the ability to stay focused.
  • SC 1 Athletes formulate a small goal for training and explain why it matters to them.
  • SC 2 Simulated stress situation (e.g. competition simulation). Children consciously use techniques (e.g. breathing) to reach 'green'.
  • SC Athletes describe a best performance: 'How did you feel?': identify and apply the characteristics of the personal optimal performance state.
  • SC 1 For each category, process goals and ranking goals (evaluate and adjust later).
  • SC 2 Consciously use breathing techniques during training and competition to stay calm.
  • SC 3 Mentally rehearse the sequence before a technique task.
  • SC 1 For each category, process goals and ranking goals (evaluate and adjust later).
  • SC 2 Use positive self-talk in a difficult task (e.g. time pressure).
  • SC 3 Perform a technique exercise with built-in distractions.
  • SC1 Apply an established mental activation routine before competition.
  • SC2 Use targeted breathing techniques or self-talk in pressure situations.
  • SC3 After a setback, consciously direct focus to the next task.
  • SC4 Deliberately visualise an upcoming competition situation.

Endurance content

Maintain an active daily life

  • Build load tolerance
  • Acquire and consolidate basic movement forms
Ausdauer F1-2

Maintain an active daily life

  • Become load-resistant
  • Apply and vary basic movement forms
Ausdauer F1-2

Maintain an active daily life

  • Load tolerance should be built extensively, in varied ways and at the same time challengingly
  • Thanks to the multi-sport orientation
  • the choice of sports remains individual and allows varied physical activity
Ausdauer F3

Preparation phase 1

  • Build foundations
  • Increase volume and frequency
  • Low to medium intensity, hardly any hard sessions
  • Varied: cycling, running, swimming, games
  • Use other sports (bike, athletics, gymnastics)

Preparation phase 2

  • Base endurance (I1)
  • Train technique deliberately
  • Speed: sprints, jumps, games
  • Running: uphill and cross
  • Cycling 60–120'

Pre-competition phase

  • Training forms from PP2 continue
  • Focus on technique
  • Roller skis, including technique courses
  • Running with poles
  • Games and relays
  • Rolling terrain

Competition phase:

  • Base and technique training on
  • snow despite performance dips
  • Use the snow period (approx. 6 months) intensively
  • Control form through competitions
  • Lots of time on snow and skis
  • Games and coordination
  • Train downhills
Ausdauer T1Ausdauer T2

Preparation phase 1

  • Build foundations
  • Increase volume and frequency
  • Low to medium intensity, hardly any hard sessions

Preparation phase 2

  • Threshold training complementing the base work
  • Targeted I2, e.g. in the technique domain
  • Integrate capacity training after the threshold block
  • Depending on the athlete profile, balance capacity vs. threshold training
  • Second half often: one threshold and one capacity session per week

Pre-competition phase

  • Most training forms continue
  • Form control through short intervals

Competition phase:

  • Base work and technique on snow despite performance dips
  • Use the snow period (approx. 6 months)
  • Form control with short and combined intervals during dense competition periods
Ausdauer T3-4

Preparation phase 1

  • Volume 18–22h per week
  • Endurance training on foot and on roller skis, complemented by cycling, rowing, swimming
  • 2 intensive sessions per week (I4 and I5) on foot or roller skis

Preparation phase 2

  • Develop VO₂max and base endurance
  • Summer competitions
  • Endurance and interval training on the roller-ski track

Pre-competition phase

  • Race intensity and VO₂max
  • Training on snow and skis

Competition phase:

  • Deliver competition performance
  • Tapering
Ausdauer E1-2
  • Development of individual needs
  • Training load and volume at world-class level
  • Specific training devices
  • VO₂max, lactate tolerance, threshold speed
  • Pace endurance, high-speed technique

Classic technique

Discover the element of snow

  • Gliding
  • Pushing
  • Skidding
  • Turning
  • Jumping
  • Balancing

Klassisch

Discover the snow playfully and move with variety on cross-country skis.
Game forms and varied exercises that promote versatile movement types. Elephant wash, skills park, name memory, the fox goes round, tag games, etc.

Ski and brake safely and independently

Classic stride (leg work)

  • Extension of the push-off leg
  • stable gliding on the gliding ski

Diagonal stride

Alternating leg and arm work in a diagonal movement for propulsion.

Herringbone

  • Scissor steps uphill: skis in a V
  • kick from the legs (no gliding)

Double poling

  • Plant both poles simultaneously
  • bring the body forward and actively extend the arms

Step turning

  • Sideways stepping along a curved line
  • weight on the outside ski

Track change

  • Lift skis parallel
  • shift weight and settle gently into the new track

Exercises

  • Stepping over roots
  • picking raspberries
  • Mexican wave
  • rocking shoes
  • etc
Klassisch
–
Skating technique

Discover the element of snow

  • Gliding
  • Pushing
  • Skidding
  • Turning
  • Jumping
  • Balancing
  • Braking on gliding devices (cross-country skis, snowboard or skis)
Skating

Discover the snow playfully and move with variety on cross-country skis.
Game forms and varied exercises that promote versatile movement types. Elephant wash, skills park, name memory, the fox goes round, tag games, etc.

Ski and brake safely and independently

  • Skating step (leg work) Extension of the push-off leg (sideways)
  • stable gliding on the gliding ski

1:2
Skating step with double poling on every second leg push.

1:1
Skating step with double poling on every leg push.

Asymmetric skate

Asymmetric arm work (lead arm) and simultaneous planting of pole and ski (otherwise like 1:2)

Diagonal skate

Leg step (sideways) with diagonal pole use.

Skating step without poles

Low centre of gravity with dynamic weight shift for longer gliding.

Exercises

  • Touch ankles
  • fences
  • bell ringer
  • hip-hopper
  • etc

Recovery April to mid-May
–

Goals

Ensure physical and mental recovery after the competition season and revive the joy of multi-sport movement.

Content

  • Unstructured
  • playful everyday movement (cycling, swimming, game sports) with clearly reduced training volume and no biathlon-specific content (shooting paused)

Goals

Ensure recovery from the competition season and keep the joy of sport alive through multi-sport movement.

Content

  • Unstructured
  • varied activities without biathlon-specific content (cycling, swimming, game sports) at clearly reduced volume; shooting training paused

Goals

Ensure physical and mental recovery after the competition season and maintain training enjoyment through multi-sport movement.

Content

  • Unstructured
  • varied activities without biathlon-specific content (cycling, swimming, game sports) at clearly reduced volume; shooting training paused

Goals

Ensure physical and mental recovery after the intensive competition season and prevent load monotony through multi-sport movement.

Content

  • Unstructured
  • varied activities without biathlon-specific content (cycling, swimming, game sports) at clearly reduced volume and low intensity; shooting training paused

Goals

Ensure physical and mental recovery after the intensive competition season and prevent load monotony and overtraining.

Content

  • Unstructured
  • varied activities without biathlon-specific content (cycling, swimming, game sports) at clearly reduced volume and low intensity; shooting training paused

Goals

Ensure physical and mental recovery after the international competition season and prevent overtraining.

Content

  • Unstructured
  • varied activities without biathlon-specific content (cycling, swimming, game sports) at clearly reduced volume and low intensity; shooting training paused

Goals

Ensure physical and mental recovery after the World Cup season and prevent overtraining at the highest load level.

Content

  • Unstructured
  • varied activities without biathlon-specific content (cycling, swimming, game sports) at clearly reduced volume and low intensity; shooting training paused
Preparation phase 1 Mid-May to August

Develop basic movement and game forms

  • Extensive
  • varied and challenging

Goals

  • Build load tolerance extensively and in varied ways
  • consolidate athletic basics (coordination, mobility, basic strength) and introduce shooting playfully

Content

  • Multi-sport athletic training (~6.4 h/week) with running drills
  • jumps
  • bodyweight exercises
  • barbell technique and first roller-ski sessions to learn basic classic and skating movements
  • complemented by playful shooting forms with the air rifle

Goals

  • Broadly build training foundations
  • increase volume and frequency
  • encourage cross-sport versatility and develop basic shooting technique (position, breathing, trigger) with the air rifle

Content

  • Athletic training focusing on barbell technique
  • core stability and first jump forms (~6.2 h/week)
  • combined with cycling
  • running
  • swimming and complementary sports such as athletics or gymnastics
  • plus regular air-rifle shooting training prone and standing

Goals

  • Broadly build training foundations
  • raise volume and frequency to a clearly higher level and automate shooting technique with the small-bore rifle

Content

  • Multi-sport athletic training with barbell technique
  • core stability and jump school (~7.7 h/week)
  • combined with cycling
  • running
  • swimming and complementary sports
  • plus systematic small-bore shooting training (position, pressure point, trigger control) prone and standing

Goals

  • Build conditioning foundations broadly and sustainably
  • increase volume and frequency at a high level and refine technical shooting elements with the small-bore rifle

Content

  • Multi-sport athletic training (~9.1 h/week) focusing on functional efficiency
  • barbell technique
  • plyometrics and core strength
  • combined with base endurance on the bike
  • running and roller skis at low to medium intensity
  • plus smooth re-cocking and stable trigger control in shooting training

Goals

  • Build conditioning foundations broadly and sustainably
  • increase volume and frequency at a high level and further refine technical shooting elements

Content

  • Extensive athletic training (~9.8 h/week) focusing on functional efficiency
  • barbell technique
  • plyometrics and core strength
  • combined with base endurance on the bike
  • running and roller skis at low to medium intensity
  • plus refinement of prone and standing shooting technique

Goals

Build conditioning foundations at a high volume level (18–22 h/week) broadly and sustainably and automate technical shooting elements.

Content

  • Endurance training on foot and on roller skis
  • complemented by cycling
  • rowing and swimming
  • combined with two intensive sessions per week (I4/I5)
  • athletic training (~11.7 h/week) focusing on barbell technique
  • plyometrics and core strength
  • plus high-frequency shooting training to automate technique

Goals

Build conditioning foundations at the highest volume level (18–22 h/week) broadly and sustainably and automate technical shooting elements.

Content

  • Endurance training on foot and on roller skis
  • complemented by cycling
  • rowing and swimming
  • combined with two intensive sessions per week (I4/I5)
  • athletic training (~13.4 h/week) focusing on barbell technique
  • plyometrics and core strength
  • plus high-frequency shooting training to automate technique

Goals

  • Develop conditioning foundations to world-class level
  • target individual needs and automate shooting technique under competition conditions

Content

  • High-volume endurance training on foot and on roller skis with specific training devices
  • complemented by cycling
  • rowing and swimming
  • athletic training (~14.2 h/week) focusing on barbell technique
  • plyometrics and core strength
  • plus individualised shooting training at the highest frequency
Preparation phase 2 September to October

Develop basic movement and game forms

  • Extensive
  • varied and challenging

Goals

  • Consolidate sport-specific movement quality on roller skis
  • use the speed/agility windows deliberately and take up the shooting position confidently

Content

  • Increased share of roller skiing (classic and skating) focusing on leg push
  • double poling and 1:2 technique
  • complemented by sprint
  • coordination and jump forms
  • advanced strength training and regular shooting training focused on position stability

Goals

  • Consolidate base endurance (I1) and sport-specific technique
  • develop speed and muscle mass deliberately and increasingly combine shooting with physical load

Content

  • Structured endurance sessions (mountain and cross running, cycling 60–120')
  • roller skiing with technique focus plus muscle building
  • first explosive strength work
  • core strength and shooting training with first combined running/shooting forms

Goals

  • Deliberately develop base endurance (I1)
  • sport-specific technique and muscle mass
  • use speed according to the window of opportunity (especially in boys) and improve shooting precision under load

Content

  • Structured endurance sessions (mountain and cross running, cycling 60–120')
  • roller skiing with technique focus
  • muscle building
  • first explosive strength work and core strength
  • plus regular combined running/roller-ski + shooting sessions

Goals

  • Deliberately develop threshold
  • capacity and maximum strength
  • sharpen the individual athlete profile and increase shooting speed and precision under load

Content

  • Structured threshold blocks (I2/I3) complemented by capacity training
  • muscle hypertrophy and intramuscular coordination training
  • combined with roller-ski technique
  • first summer competitions (Swiss Biathlon Cup) and combined sessions focusing on shooting speed and 30/30 precision

Goals

  • Deliberately develop threshold
  • capacity and maximum strength
  • further sharpen the individual athlete profile and increase shooting speed and precision under competition load

Content

  • Structured threshold blocks (I2/I3) complemented by capacity training
  • muscle hypertrophy and intramuscular coordination training
  • combined with roller-ski technique
  • summer competitions (Swiss Biathlon Cup, IBU Junior Cup) and combined sessions with shooting speed and 30/30 precision

Goals

  • Deliberately develop VO₂max and base endurance
  • further build muscle hypertrophy and maximum strength and standardise shooting speed

Content

  • Endurance and interval training on the roller-ski track
  • complemented by summer competitions (Swiss Biathlon Cup, IBU Cup)
  • intramuscular coordination training and explosive strength with additional weights
  • plus high-intensity combined sessions (running/roller skis + shooting) with standardised shooting speed

Goals

  • Deliberately develop VO₂max and base endurance
  • further build muscle hypertrophy and maximum strength and standardise shooting speed

Content

  • Endurance and interval training on the roller-ski track
  • complemented by national/international summer competitions (IBU Summer World Cup, Swiss Biathlon Cup)
  • intramuscular coordination training and explosive strength with additional weights
  • plus high-intensity combined sessions with standardised shooting speed

Goals

  • Develop VO₂max
  • lactate tolerance and threshold speed to world-class level
  • further build muscle hypertrophy and maximum strength and secure shooting speed under World Cup conditions

Content

  • Endurance and interval training on the roller-ski track
  • complemented by national/international summer competitions
  • intramuscular coordination training and explosive strength with additional weights
  • plus individualised combined sessions at World Cup shooting speed
Pre-competition phase November

Develop basic movement and game forms

  • Extensive
  • varied and challenging

Goals

  • Manage the transition from roller skis to snow
  • establish playful
  • confident movement on cross-country skis (classic and skating) and automate the switch from skiing to shooting

Content

  • First on-snow sessions with game forms (elephant wash, tag games, skills park)
  • basic techniques (diagonal stride, herringbone, step turning, 1:2)
  • maintaining athleticism through short
  • intensive sessions and varied jumps
  • plus first combined skiing + shooting forms at the biathlon facility

Goals

  • Refine technique on roller skis and snow
  • prepare the transition to the snow season and stabilise shooting under skiing load

Content

  • Technique courses on roller skis
  • running with poles in rolling terrain
  • games and relays
  • explosive strength and core strength training
  • plus combined skiing + shooting sessions focused on a stable position technique after load

Goals

  • Refine technique on roller skis and snow
  • develop explosive strength
  • prepare the transition to the snow season and stabilise shooting speed under skiing load

Content

  • Technique courses on roller skis
  • running with poles in rolling terrain
  • games and relays
  • explosive strength and core strength training
  • plus combined skiing + shooting sessions focused on shooting speed and precision

Goals

  • Control form through short intervals
  • bring maximum and speed strength to season level and secure shooting performance under competition conditions

Content

  • Continuation of all training forms with emphasis on short intervals
  • speed and explosive strength with and without additional weight
  • transition to snow with technique focus
  • plus competition-like combined sessions focused on shooting stability and speed

Goals

  • Control form through short intervals
  • bring maximum and speed strength to season level and secure shooting performance under competition conditions

Content

  • Continuation of all training forms with emphasis on short intervals
  • speed and explosive strength with and without additional weight
  • transition to snow with technique focus
  • plus competition-like combined sessions focused on shooting stability and speed

Goals

  • Bring race intensity and VO₂max to competition level
  • adapt to snow and secure shooting performance at race pace

Content

  • On-snow and ski training with race-pace intervals
  • complemented by speed and explosive strength training
  • core strength
  • plus competition-like combined sessions with shooting performance at race pace

Goals

  • Bring race intensity and VO₂max to World Cup level
  • adapt to snow and secure shooting performance under World Cup conditions

Content

  • On-snow and ski training with race-pace intervals
  • complemented by speed and explosive strength training
  • core strength
  • plus competition-like combined sessions with shooting performance at World Cup pace

Goals

  • Bring pace endurance and high-speed technique to World Cup level
  • adapt to snow and keep shooting performance constant under World Cup conditions

Content

  • On-snow and ski training with race-pace intervals
  • complemented by speed and explosive strength training
  • core strength
  • plus individualised combined sessions with constant shooting performance at World Cup pace
Competition phase December to March

Develop basic movement and game forms

  • Extensive
  • varied and challenging

Goals

  • Gather first competition experience in a joyful
  • learning-oriented environment
  • apply the movement quality built in summer on snow and experience shooting in competition

Content

  • Regular on-snow training with technical variety
  • participation in the Swiss Biathlon Cup - Kids and local events
  • complemented by reduced athletic training (~2.6 h/week) for strength maintenance and injury prevention
  • plus competition-like shooting exercises

Goals

  • Use the roughly six months on snow intensively for technique and basics
  • gain experience through regional competitions and consolidate shooting in competition

Content

  • Lots of time on skis focusing on technique
  • downhills
  • games and coordination
  • complemented by maintenance athletic and core training (~2.6 h/week)
  • reduced explosive strength training
  • plyometrics and national-level competitions

Goals

  • Use the roughly six months on snow intensively for technique and basics
  • gain experience through regional and international competitions and consolidate shooting performance in competition

Content

  • Lots of time on skis focusing on technique
  • downhills
  • games and coordination
  • complemented by maintenance athletic and core training (~2.6 h/week)
  • explosive strength and plyometrics at reduced volume
  • plus national-level competitions and first international starts

Goals

Use the roughly six months on snow for form and performance management in a dense competition calendar and stabilise shooting performance in international competition.

Content

  • Lots of time on skis with base and technique training despite performance dips
  • form control through short and combined intervals
  • maintenance athletic
  • explosive and maximum strength training (~2.6 h/week) with volume adapted to competitions
  • plus starts in international competitions

Goals

Use the roughly six months on snow for targeted form and performance management in the dense international calendar and stabilise shooting performance in international competition.

Content

  • Lots of time on skis with base and technique training despite performance dips
  • form control through short and combined intervals
  • maintenance athletic
  • explosive and maximum strength training (~3.3 h/week) with volume adapted to competitions
  • plus starts in international competitions and series

Goals

  • Deliver competition performance in the international calendar
  • control form through targeted tapering and keep shooting performance constant under World Cup conditions

Content

  • Competition-oriented ski training with individual load management
  • combined with maintenance athletic
  • explosive and maximum strength training (~3.8 h/week) at constant intensity and volume adapted to competitions
  • plus World Cup starts

Goals

  • Deliver competition performance in the top international calendar
  • control form through targeted tapering and keep shooting performance constant under World Cup conditions

Content

  • Competition-oriented ski training with individual load management
  • combined with maintenance athletic
  • explosive and maximum strength training (~4.3 h/week) at constant intensity and volume adapted to competitions
  • plus starts in the World Cup
  • at World Championships and at the Olympic Games

Goals

  • Consistently deliver performance in the top international calendar
  • control form through targeted tapering and produce shooting performance at the highest level under World Cup conditions

Content

  • Competition-oriented ski training with highly individualised load management
  • combined with maintenance athletic
  • explosive and maximum strength training (~4.6 h/week) at constant intensity and volume adapted to competitions
  • plus starts in the World Cup
  • at World Championships and at the Olympic Games

  • SC 1 Children estimate how much they should drink per training session and check it (e.g. with markings on the water bottle).
  • SC 2 Children independently check that all important items are packed (bag check).
  • SC Document and discuss one day of nutrition: food, drinks and snacks.
  • SC Independently put together a meal/snack for before, during and after training/competition and discuss it.
  • SC Experiment with different snacks, hydration strategies or meals before/during/after training/competition and adapt them individually.
  • SC 1 Test nutrition and hydration under competition conditions (e.g. gels, isotonic drinks during exertion).
  • SC 2 Document and evaluate fluid loss, energy needs and recovery.
  • SC Established nutrition and hydration strategy for training and competition.

Balanced diet

  • ½ vegetables/fruit
  • ¼ carbohydrates
  • ¼ protein at every meal

Drinking

  • Water as the main drink
  • approx
  • 1.5–2 l daily

Regular meals

Preparation

Bring snacks and water bottle to training.

Nutrition

Goal

  • Strengthen awareness and adaptation
  • deepen understanding of macronutrients (carbohydrates, protein, fat) and fluid needs

Before training

  • Drink approx
  • 500 ml of water 1–2h beforehand
  • In heat or with high salt loss use slightly salty drinks (1 pinch of salt)

During training

Drink 150–200 ml every 15–20'; for efforts >1h add carbohydrates (e.g. diluted fruit juices, carbohydrate-rich drinks).

After training

  • 0.5-1 l of fluid within 30'
  • After intensive efforts use a protein shake
  • recovery drink
  • electrolyte drinks or slightly salty water

Advanced knowledge of micronutrients (vitamins, minerals) and their role in performance.

Nutrition

Before training

  • 2–3h beforehand: carbohydrate-rich
  • easily digestible meal (e.g. wholegrain bread with honey)
  • 30' beforehand: small snack (e.g. banana)

During training (>1h exertion)

30–60 g of carbohydrates per hour (e.g. energy bar, dried fruit)

After training

Within 30': snack with carbohydrates and protein (e.g. yoghurt with fruit, milkshake).

Main meal

  • balanced with carbohydrates (e.g. rice, pasta)
  • protein (e.g. chicken, lentils) and vegetables

Skills-Check (SC)
  • SC Questions for the children: how many hours of sleep do we need? What helps us sleep better?
  • SC For one week, document sleep duration and how they feel the next day.
  • SC Try breathing techniques or progressive muscle relaxation (PMR) before sleep.
  • SC 1 Document sleep duration and quality for one week, together with training performance.
  • SC 2 Reflect on evening routines and make adjustments.
  • SC 1 Create and implement a plan for sleep and meal times before a competition.
  • SC 2 'Park' thoughts before sleep, e.g. by writing them down or with breathing exercises (rumination stop)
  • SC Established sleep routine for training and competition.
Content

Sleep duration

8–10h/night
Sleep supports concentration, energy and recovery.

Sleep

Sleep duration

8–10h/night

Routine

Same bedtimes, also at weekends.

Relaxation

  • Avoid screens 1h before sleep
  • introduce rituals such as reading or breathing exercises

Sleep environment

  • Dark
  • cool
  • quiet (16–18°C)
Sleep

Regular sleep times

Build in relaxation rituals

Thought stop

  • Get up if awake for a long time
  • Write down thoughts to clear the mind
  • Turn negative thoughts about sleep into positive beliefs

Optimised use of caffeine and aids

  • Consider the effect (half-life 6h, stronger effect in adolescents)
  • avoid at least 6h before sleep
  • Use eye masks
  • ear protection
  • etc

Plan power naps

  • Short naps of 10–15' for recovery
  • ideally after lunch

Adjustments for travel and competitions

  • Adapt sleep and meal times to time zone changes
  • Use strategies against jet lag
Sleep
  • Targeted
  • individual sleep optimisation secures long-term performance

Regular sleep routines and adaptation to travel or competitions are decisive.

  • Sleep problems should be monitored and treated if necessary
  • Power naps and relaxation techniques such as the thought stop promote recovery and mental calm

Skills-Checks (SC) mental skills
  • SC Athletes talk about a moment they are proud of.
  • SC Athletes describe their emotions in difficult situations (e.g. after a mistake) using a traffic light.

Red

I am angry.

Yellow

I am unsure.

Green

I am calm/focused.

  • SC Athletes perform a task (e.g. technique exercise) with distractions (e.g. noise): test the ability to stay focused.
  • SC 1 Athletes formulate a small goal for training and explain why it matters to them.
  • SC 2 Simulated stress situation (e.g. competition simulation). Children consciously use techniques (e.g. breathing) to reach 'green'.
  • SC Athletes describe a best performance: 'How did you feel?': identify and apply the characteristics of the personal optimal performance state.
  • SC 1 For each category, process goals and ranking goals (evaluate and adjust later).
  • SC 2 Consciously use breathing techniques during training and competition to stay calm.
  • SC 3 Mentally rehearse the sequence before a technique task.
  • SC 1 For each category, process goals and ranking goals (evaluate and adjust later).
  • SC 2 Use positive self-talk in a difficult task (e.g. time pressure).
  • SC 3 Perform a technique exercise with built-in distractions.
  • SC1 Apply an established mental activation routine before competition.
  • SC2 Use targeted breathing techniques or self-talk in pressure situations.
  • SC3 After a setback, consciously direct focus to the next task.
  • SC4 Deliberately visualise an upcoming competition situation.

Endurance content

Maintain an active daily life

  • Build load tolerance
  • Acquire and consolidate basic movement forms
Ausdauer F1-2

Maintain an active daily life

  • Become load-resistant
  • Apply and vary basic movement forms
Ausdauer F1-2

Maintain an active daily life

  • Load tolerance should be built extensively, in varied ways and at the same time challengingly
  • Thanks to the multi-sport orientation
  • the choice of sports remains individual and allows varied physical activity
Ausdauer F3

Preparation phase 1

  • Build foundations
  • Increase volume and frequency
  • Low to medium intensity, hardly any hard sessions
  • Varied: cycling, running, swimming, games
  • Use other sports (bike, athletics, gymnastics)

Preparation phase 2

  • Base endurance (I1)
  • Train technique deliberately
  • Speed: sprints, jumps, games
  • Running: uphill and cross
  • Cycling 60–120'

Pre-competition phase

  • Training forms from PP2 continue
  • Focus on technique
  • Roller skis, including technique courses
  • Running with poles
  • Games and relays
  • Rolling terrain

Competition phase:

  • Base and technique training on
  • snow despite performance dips
  • Use the snow period (approx. 6 months) intensively
  • Control form through competitions
  • Lots of time on snow and skis
  • Games and coordination
  • Train downhills
Ausdauer T1Ausdauer T2

Preparation phase 1

  • Build foundations
  • Increase volume and frequency
  • Low to medium intensity, hardly any hard sessions

Preparation phase 2

  • Threshold training complementing the base work
  • Targeted I2, e.g. in the technique domain
  • Integrate capacity training after the threshold block
  • Depending on the athlete profile, balance capacity vs. threshold training
  • Second half often: one threshold and one capacity session per week

Pre-competition phase

  • Most training forms continue
  • Form control through short intervals

Competition phase:

  • Base work and technique on snow despite performance dips
  • Use the snow period (approx. 6 months)
  • Form control with short and combined intervals during dense competition periods
Ausdauer T3-4

Preparation phase 1

  • Volume 18–22h per week
  • Endurance training on foot and on roller skis, complemented by cycling, rowing, swimming
  • 2 intensive sessions per week (I4 and I5) on foot or roller skis

Preparation phase 2

  • Develop VO₂max and base endurance
  • Summer competitions
  • Endurance and interval training on the roller-ski track

Pre-competition phase

  • Race intensity and VO₂max
  • Training on snow and skis

Competition phase:

  • Deliver competition performance
  • Tapering
Ausdauer E1-2
  • Development of individual needs
  • Training load and volume at world-class level
  • Specific training devices
  • VO₂max, lactate tolerance, threshold speed
  • Pace endurance, high-speed technique
Ausdauer M

Classic technique

Discover the element of snow

Klassisch

Discover the snow playfully and move with variety on cross-country skis.
Game forms and varied exercises that promote versatile movement types. Elephant wash, skills park, name memory, the fox goes round, tag games, etc.

Ski and brake safely and independently

Classic stride (leg work)

  • Extension of the push-off leg
  • stable gliding on the gliding ski

Diagonal stride

Alternating leg and arm work in a diagonal movement for propulsion.

Herringbone

  • Scissor steps uphill: skis in a V
  • kick from the legs (no gliding)

Double poling

  • Plant both poles simultaneously
  • bring the body forward and actively extend the arms

Step turning

  • Sideways stepping along a curved line
  • weight on the outside ski

Track change

  • Lift skis parallel
  • shift weight and settle gently into the new track

Exercises

  • Stepping over roots
  • picking raspberries
  • Mexican wave
  • rocking shoes
  • etc

Game forms and varied exercises that promote versatile movement types. Elephant wash, skills park, name memory, the fox goes round, tag games, etc.

Ski and brake safely and independently

  • Skating step (leg work) Extension of the push-off leg (sideways)
  • stable gliding on the gliding ski

1:2
Skating step with double poling on every second leg push.

1:1
Skating step with double poling on every leg push.

Asymmetric skate

Asymmetric arm work (lead arm) and simultaneous planting of pole and ski (otherwise like 1:2)

Diagonal skate

Leg step (sideways) with diagonal pole use.

Skating step without poles

Low centre of gravity with dynamic weight shift for longer gliding.

Exercises

  • Touch ankles
  • fences
  • bell ringer
  • hip-hopper
  • etc

Preparation phase 1 (VP1): mid-May-July

Develop basic movement and game forms

  • Extensive
  • varied and challenging
–

Goals

  • Build strong and resilient musculature
  • Develop a good aerobic base
  • Promote coordinative abilities
  • Variation of training methods
  • Technique development

Content

  • Ski jumping technique training (various training forms)
  • strength endurance (no weights, high repetition count)
  • muscle building (moderate weights, approx. ten repetitions)
  • plyometrics (high repetition count)
  • Easy endurance sessions (running, cycling, inline)
  • Injury prevention (leg axis stability, mobility, core strength, hamstring strengthening)
  • varied training focusing on coordination and strength

Content

–
Preparation phase 2 (VP2): Aug-Oct

Develop basic movement and game forms

  • Extensive
  • varied and challenging
–

Goals

  • Build speed
  • speed strength and explosive strength
  • Transfer base endurance into playful short interval forms
  • balance between recovery and load
  • Technique development

Content

Ski jumping technique training (specific, high repetition count), sprint forms, plyometrics (jump forms, low repetition count), strength building (medium to low repetition counts, little weight), interval runs, deliberately include recovery phases (school holidays).
Injury prevention (leg axis stability, mobility, core strength, hamstring strengthening), specific training focusing on technique.

Goals

  • Build speed
  • speed strength and explosive strength
  • Balance between recovery and load
  • Technique optimisation

Content

  • Ski jumping technique training (specific, high repetition count)
  • sprint forms
  • plyometrics (jump forms, low repetition count)
  • maximum strength building (high to maximum weights, medium to low repetition counts)
  • interval runs
  • deliberately include recovery phases
  • Injury prevention (leg axis stability, mobility, core strength, hamstring strengthening)
  • specific training focusing on technique
–
Pre-competition phase (VWP): Nov

Develop basic movement and game forms

  • Extensive
  • varied and challenging
–

Goals

  • Maintain speed and explosive strength
  • Stay healthy and mentally strong

Content

  • Plyometrics (jump forms, low repetition count)
  • speed strength building (low repetition counts)
  • coordination training (cross-country skiing)
  • focus on stabilisation
  • mobilisation and imitation training

Goals

  • Maintain speed and explosive strength
  • Stay healthy and mentally strong
  • Quality before quantity
  • Transfer from summer to winter hill

Content

  • Plyometrics (jump forms, low repetition count)
  • maximum strength building (high to maximum weights, medium to low repetition counts)
  • imitations
  • focus on coolness and precision
–
Competition phase (WP): Dec-Apr

Develop basic movement and game forms

  • Extensive
  • varied and challenging
–

Goals

  • Develop enjoyment of competition
  • maintain strength and speed training
  • balance recovery and load
  • As many snow jumps as possible (use snow-rich phases)

Content

  • Strength and speed training
  • Bring training performance into competition

Goals

  • Competitions steer the training
  • Prioritise competitions (important, medium, minor)
  • Plan training blocks with recovery in mind
  • maintain strength and speed training
  • balance recovery and load

Content

  • Targeted competition preparation
  • Strength and speed training
  • Clear recovery phases

Skills-Checks (SC) nutrition
  • SC 1 Children estimate how much they should drink per training session and check it (e.g. with markings on the water bottle).
  • SC 2 Children independently check that all important items are packed (bag check).
  • SC Document and discuss one day of nutrition: food, drinks and snacks.
  • SC Independently put together a meal/snack for before, during and after training/competition and discuss it.
  • SC Experiment with different snacks, hydration strategies or meals before/during/after training/competition and adapt them individually.
  • SC 1 Test nutrition and hydration under competition conditions (e.g. gels, isotonic drinks during exertion).
  • SC 2 Document and evaluate fluid loss, energy needs and recovery.
  • SC Established nutrition and hydration strategy for training and competition.

Nutrition

Goal

  • Strengthen awareness and adaptation
  • deepen understanding of macronutrients (carbohydrates, protein, fat) and fluid needs

Before training

  • Drink approx
  • 500 ml of water 1–2h beforehand
  • In heat or with high salt loss use slightly salty drinks (1 pinch of salt)

During training

Drink 150–200 ml every 15–20'; for efforts >1h add carbohydrates (e.g. diluted fruit juices, carbohydrate-rich drinks).

After training

  • 0.5-1 l of fluid within 30'
  • After intensive efforts use a protein shake
  • recovery drink
  • electrolyte drinks or slightly salty water
Nutrition

Nutrition

Before training

  • 2–3h beforehand: carbohydrate-rich
  • easily digestible meal (e.g. wholegrain bread with honey)
  • 30' beforehand: small snack (e.g. banana)

During training (>1h exertion)

30–60 g of carbohydrates per hour (e.g. energy bar, dried fruit)

After training

Within 30': snack with carbohydrates and protein (e.g. yoghurt with fruit, milkshake).

Main meal

  • balanced with carbohydrates (e.g. rice, pasta)
  • protein (e.g. chicken, lentils) and vegetables

Skills-Checks (SC) sleep
  • SC Questions for the children: how many hours of sleep do we need? What helps us sleep better?
  • SC For one week, document sleep duration and how they feel the next day.
  • SC Try breathing techniques or progressive muscle relaxation (PMR) before sleep.
  • SC 1 Document sleep duration and quality for one week, together with training performance.
  • SC 2 Reflect on evening routines and make adjustments.
  • SC 1 Create and implement a plan for sleep and meal times before a competition.
  • SC 2 'Park' thoughts before sleep, e.g. by writing them down or with breathing exercises (rumination stop)
  • SC Established sleep routine for training and competition.
Sleep content

Sleep duration

8–10h/night
Sleep supports concentration, energy and recovery.

Sleep

Sleep duration

8–10h/night

Routine

Same bedtimes, also at weekends.

Relaxation

  • Avoid screens 1h before sleep
  • introduce rituals such as reading or breathing exercises

Sleep environment

  • Dark
  • cool
  • quiet (16–18°C)
Sleep

Regular sleep times

Build in relaxation rituals

Thought stop

  • Get up if awake for a long time
  • Write down thoughts to clear the mind
  • Turn negative thoughts about sleep into positive beliefs

Optimised use of caffeine and aids

  • Consider the effect (half-life 6h, stronger effect in adolescents)
  • avoid at least 6h before sleep
  • Use eye masks
  • ear protection
  • etc

Plan power naps

  • Short naps of 10–15' for recovery
  • ideally after lunch

Adjustments for travel and competitions

  • Adapt sleep and meal times to time zone changes
  • Use strategies against jet lag
Sleep
  • Targeted
  • individual sleep optimisation secures long-term performance

Regular sleep routines and adaptation to travel or competitions are decisive.

  • Sleep problems should be monitored and treated if necessary
  • Power naps and relaxation techniques such as the thought stop promote recovery and mental calm

Skills-Checks (SC) mental skills
  • SC Athletes talk about a moment they are proud of.
  • SC Athletes describe their emotions in difficult situations (e.g. after a mistake) using a traffic light.

Red

I am angry.

Yellow

I am unsure.

Green

I am calm/focused.

  • SC Athletes perform a task (e.g. technique exercise) with distractions (e.g. noise): test the ability to stay focused.
  • SC 1 Athletes formulate a small goal for training and explain why it matters to them.
  • SC 2 Simulated stress situation (e.g. competition simulation). Children consciously use techniques (e.g. breathing) to reach 'green'.
  • SC Athletes describe a best performance: 'How did you feel?': identify and apply the characteristics of the personal optimal performance state.
  • SC 1 For each category, process goals and ranking goals (evaluate and adjust later).
  • SC 2 Consciously use breathing techniques during training and competition to stay calm.
  • SC 3 Mentally rehearse the sequence before a technique task.
  • SC 1 For each category, process goals and ranking goals (evaluate and adjust later).
  • SC 2 Use positive self-talk in a difficult task (e.g. time pressure).
  • SC 3 Perform a technique exercise with built-in distractions.
  • SC1 Apply an established mental activation routine before competition.
  • SC2 Use targeted breathing techniques or self-talk in pressure situations.
  • SC3 After a setback, consciously direct focus to the next task.
  • SC4 Deliberately visualise an upcoming competition situation.

Kraft F1-2

Summer

  • Bodyweight exercises through the full range of motion
  • Core stability
  • Leg axis stability
  • Varied jumps
  • Foot arch development

Winter

  • Speed and explosive strength in the form of jumps
  • Further strength building
Kraft F3

Preparation phase 1

  • Barbell technique with wooden stick and light weights
  • Local muscular endurance with bodyweight
  • Extensive jump variations (barefoot for foot arch development)
  • Core training with plank variations (adduction and abduction for leg axis stability)

Preparation phase 2

  • Muscle building
  • Building up explosive strength training
  • Intensive jump variations
  • Core training

Pre-competition phase

  • Muscle building
  • Explosive strength training
  • Specific jump forms
  • Core training

Competition phase

  • Explosive strength training
  • Specific jump forms at reduced volume
  • Core training

* Window of opportunity in girls T1
* Window of opportunity in boys T2

Kraft T1Kraft T2

Preparation phase 1

  • Sensorimotor strength training
  • Barbell technique with light to moderate weight
  • Muscle building and prehab exercises (leg axis stability, hamstring strengthening, foot arch development)
  • Extensive jump variations
  • Core training

Preparation phase 2

  • Maintaining the built-up musculature
  • Increasing maximum strength through intramuscular coordination training
  • Explosive strength training with additional resistance or assistance
  • Intensive jump variations
  • Core training

Pre-competition phase

  • Increasing maximum strength
  • Explosive strength with and without additional load
  • Specific jump forms
  • Core training

Competition phase

  • Maintain explosive and maximum strength
  • Adapting volume to competitions
  • Specific jump forms at reduced volume and high intensity

Preparation phase 1 (VP1): mid-May-July

Goals

  • build strong and resilient musculature
  • Develop a good aerobic base
  • Promote coordinative abilities
  • Variation of training methods
  • Technique development

Content

  • ski jumping technique training (various training forms)
  • strength endurance (no weights, high repetition count)
  • muscle building (moderate weights, approx. ten repetitions)
  • plyometrics (high repetition count)
  • Easy endurance sessions (running, cycling, inline)
  • Injury prevention (leg axis stability, mobility, core strength, hamstring strengthening)
  • varied training focusing on coordination and strength

Preparation phase 2 (VP2): Aug-Oct
–

Goals

  • build speed
  • speed strength and explosive strength
  • Transfer base endurance into playful short interval forms
  • balance between recovery and load
  • Technique development

Content

ski jumping technique training (specific, high repetition count), sprint forms, plyometrics (jump forms, low repetition count), strength building (medium to low repetition counts, little weight), interval runs, deliberately include recovery phases (school holidays).
Injury prevention (leg axis stability, mobility, core strength, hamstring strengthening), specific training focusing on technique.

Goals

  • build speed
  • speed strength and explosive strength
  • Balance between recovery and load
  • Technique optimisation

Content

  • ski jumping technique training (specific, high repetition count)
  • sprint forms
  • plyometrics (jump forms, low repetition count)
  • maximum strength building (high to maximum weights, medium to low repetition counts)
  • interval runs
  • deliberately include recovery phases
  • Injury prevention (leg axis stability, mobility, core strength, hamstring strengthening)
  • specific training focusing on technique

Skills-Checks (SC) nutrition
  • SC 1 children estimate how much they should drink per training session and check it (e.g. with markings on the water bottle).
  • SC 2 children independently check that all important items are packed (bag check).
  • SC Document and discuss one day of nutrition: food, drinks and snacks.
  • SC Independently put together a meal/snack for before, during and after training/competition and discuss it.
  • SC Experiment with different snacks, hydration strategies or meals before/during/after training/competition and adapt them individually.
  • SC 1 test nutrition and hydration under competition conditions (e.g. gels, isotonic drinks during exercise).
  • SC 2 document and analyse fluid loss, energy needs and recovery.
–

Implement the sports bag checklist

Goal

  • Promote healthy everyday habits

  • energy for sport and school

Balanced diet

  • ½ vegetables/fruit
  • ¼ carbohydrates
  • ¼ protein at every meal

Drinking

  • approx
  • 1.5–2 l daily

Regular meals

Preparation

Bring snacks and water bottle to training.

Goal

Strengthen awareness and adaptation; deepen understanding of macronutrients (carbohydrates, protein, fat) and fluid needs.

Before training

  • Drink approx
  • 500 ml of water 1–2h beforehand
  • In heat or with high salt loss
  • use lightly salted drinks (1 pinch of salt)

During training

Drink 150–200 ml every 15–20'; for efforts >1h add carbohydrates (e.g. diluted fruit juices).

After training

  • 0.5-1 l of fluid within 30'
  • For intense efforts use electrolyte drinks or lightly salted water

Optimisation and individualisation

Advanced knowledge of micronutrients (vitamins, minerals) and their role in performance.

Goal

Balanced diet

  • ½ vegetables/fruit

Drinking

  • approx

Regular meals

Preparation

Bring snacks and water bottle to training.

Before training

  • 2–3h beforehand: carbohydrate-rich
  • easily digestible meal (e.g. wholegrain bread with honey)
  • 30' beforehand: small snack (e.g. banana)

During training (>1h exertion)

30–60 g of carbohydrates per hour (e.g. energy bar, dried fruit)

After training

Within 30': snack with carbohydrates and protein (e.g. yoghurt with fruit, milkshake).

Main meal

  • balanced with carbohydrates (e.g. rice, pasta)
  • protein (e.g. chicken, lentils) and vegetables

Optimisation and individualisation

Advanced knowledge of micronutrients (vitamins, minerals) and their role in performance.

Skills-Checks (SC) sleep
  • SC Questions for the children: how many hours of sleep do we need? What helps us sleep better?
  • SC For one week, document sleep duration and how they feel the next day.
  • SC Try breathing techniques or progressive muscle relaxation (PMR) before sleep.
  • SC 1 document sleep duration and quality for one week, together with training performance.
  • SC 2 reflect on evening routines and make adjustments.
  • SC 1 create and implement a plan for sleep and meal times before a competition.
  • SC 2 "park" thoughts before sleep, e.g. by writing them down or with breathing exercises (rumination stop)
–
Sleep content

Sleep duration

8–10h/night
Sleep supports concentration, energy and recovery.

Sleep duration

8–10h/night

Routine

Same bedtimes, also at weekends.

Relaxation

  • Avoid screens 1h before sleep
  • introduce rituals such as reading or breathing exercises

Sleep environment

  • Dark
  • cool
  • quiet (16–18°C)
Regeneration

Regular sleep times

Build in relaxation rituals

Rumination stop

  • Get up if awake for a long time
  • Write down thoughts to clear your head
  • Turn negative thoughts about sleep into positive beliefs

Optimised use of caffeine and aids

  • Consider the effect (half-life 6h, stronger effect in adolescents)
  • avoid at least 6h before sleep
  • Use eye masks
  • ear protection
  • etc

Plan power naps

  • Short naps of 10–15' for recovery
  • ideally after lunch

Adjustments for travel and competitions

  • Adapt sleep and meal times to time zone changes
  • Use strategies against jet lag
Regeneration

Targeted and individual sleep optimisation secures long-term performance.

Regular sleep routines and adapting to travel or competitions are decisive.

  • Sleep problems should be monitored and treated if necessary
  • Power naps and relaxation techniques such as the rumination stop promote recovery and mental calm

Skills-Checks (SC) mental skills
  • SC Athletes talk about a moment they are proud of.
  • SC Athletes describe their emotions in difficult situations (e.g. after a mistake) using a traffic light.

Red

I am angry.

Yellow

I am unsure.

Green

I am calm/focused.

  • SC Athletes perform a task (e.g. technique exercise) with distractions (e.g. noise): test the ability to stay focused.
  • SC 1 Athletes formulate a small goal for training and explain why it matters to them.
  • SC 2 Simulated stress situation (e.g. competition simulation). Children consciously use techniques (e.g. breathing) to reach 'green'.
  • SC Athletes describe a best performance: 'How did you feel?': identify and apply the characteristics of the personal optimal performance state.
  • SC 1 for each category, process goals and ranking goals (evaluate and adjust later).
  • SC 2 during e.g. interval training, consciously use breathing techniques to stay calm.
  • SC 3 before a technique task, mentally rehearse the sequence.
  • SC 1 For each category, process goals and ranking goals (evaluate and adjust later).
  • SC 2 Use positive self-talk in a difficult task (e.g. time pressure).
  • SC 3 Perform a technique exercise with built-in distractions.

Preparation phase 1 (VP1): mid-May-Aug
–

Goals

  • make the musculature strong and resilient
  • Improve barbell technique
  • Develop a good aerobic base
  • Promote coordinative abilities
  • Variation of training methods

Content

  • strength endurance (light weights, high repetition count)
  • muscle building (moderate weights, approx. ten repetitions)
  • maximum strength training towards the end of this phase
  • Plyometrics (high repetition count)
  • Long
  • easy endurance sessions (cycling, running, inline)
  • Varied training focusing on coordination
  • strength and endurance
Preparation phase 2 (VP2): Sept-Oct
–

Goals

  • build speed
  • speed strength and explosive strength
  • Transfer base endurance into intensive interval forms
  • balance between recovery and load

Content

  • sprint forms
  • plyometrics (jump forms, low repetition count)
  • strength building (high weights, medium to low repetition counts)
  • interval runs and base endurance
  • deliberately include recovery phases
Pre-competition phase (VWP): Nov
–

Goals

  • maintain speed and explosive strength
  • Use snow training for the coordinative implementation of conditioning abilities
  • Stay healthy and mentally strong

Content

  • snow training with a high volume of training runs
  • Competition simulations
  • Focus on coolness and precision
  • Base endurance for recovery
  • Maintenance strength training
Competition phase (WP): Dec-Apr
–

Goals

  • competitions steer the training
  • Prioritise competitions (important, medium, minor)
  • Plan training blocks with recovery in mind
  • maintain strength and speed training
  • balance recovery and load

Content

  • targeted competition preparation
  • Strength and speed training
  • Clear recovery phases
